_strings.@@afd7b684bbf9: Treaty conformity — PA does NOT conform to federal tax treaties: income exempt from federal tax under a treaty is STILL taxable by PA. Do not carry a federal treaty exclusion onto the state return. (This is about TREATY conformity only — a state's Internal Revenue Code conformity date and its deduction/credit conformity are separate questions; see any law-change lines below.) State note: PA does NOT start from federal adjusted gross income. Per the official Department of Revenue Personal Income Tax page and the 2023 PA-40 instructions, PA imposes a flat 3.07% tax on eight SEPARATELY-computed classes of income ("Pennsylvania taxes eight classes of income: (1) compensation; (2) interest; (3) dividends; (4) net profits...; (5) net gains...dispositions of property; (6) net gains...rents, royalties, patents and copyrights; (7) income...through estates or trusts; and (8) gambling and lottery winnings"). PA provides no standard deduction or personal exemption and the 2023 PA-40 instructions state filing requirements "are different than federal requirements." Because PA computes taxable compensation from gross PA-source wages rather than inheriting federal AGI, there is NO automatic federal-AGI pass-through that would carry a federal tax-treaty exclusion into the state return, and neither the PA-40 instructions nor the PA Personal Income Tax Guide (Brief Overview/Filing Requirements) contain any treaty pass-through mechanism. Under the task rubric this is the state-builds-income-from-scratch (not federal AGI), no-treaty-pass-through case -> conforms_to_federal_treaties = false. CAVEAT: In administrative practice PA generally does not tax compensation a federal treaty exempts (such wages typically are excluded from PA-taxable Box 16 compensation), so the precise treatment of treaty-exempt income should be confirmed with the PA DOR; flagged in unverified.

states.reason: Worked in PA in 2023 without living there — file a nonresident return on PA-source income.
warnings: Remote-work trap: work performed from TX for an employer sitting in PA, and PA HAS a convenience-of-the-employer sourcing rule. 61 Pa. Code § 109.8: "Any allowance claimed for days worked outside of this Commonwealth shall be based upon the performance of services which, of necessity, obligate the employe or casual employe to perform out-of-State duties in the service of his employer or casual employer." Out-of-state days reduce Pennsylvania-source compensation only when the employer's business NECESSITY — not the employee's convenience — puts the work out of state. Trigger: A nonresident allocating compensation from Pennsylvania-based employment between in-state and out-of-state working days. Exceptions: Days that of necessity obligate out-of-State duties in the employer's service qualify for the allowance; the regulation names no home-office factor test — necessity is the single standard. [61 Pa. Code § 109.8 (Compensation of nonresidents) — operative allowance sentence transcribed verbatim. — https://www.pacodeandbulletin.gov/Display/pacode?file=/secure/pacode/data/061/chapter109/s109.8.html] If the rule reaches these wages, a NONRESIDENT PA return is required that the physical footprint alone never shows.

state_tax.work_common_tail: . Tax line: PA-40 Line 12 (PA Tax Liability) = Line 11 (Adjusted PA Taxable Income = Line 9 minus Line 10) x 3.07 percent (0.0307). This op computes the state's flat-rate tax line ONLY — county/city add-on taxes, state credits, and any amounts outside the rate schedule are NOT modeled. Pack notes: PA does NOT start from federal AGI: it taxes eight SEPARATELY-computed classes of income (Lines 1a-8 — compensation; interest; dividends and capital gains distributions; net business/profession/farm income; net gains from disposition of property; net rents/royalties/patents/copyrights; estate or trust income; gambling and lottery winnings). A loss in one class may never offset income in another class. "PA law does not allow standard deductions, deductions for personal exemptions, itemized deductions or deductions for personal expenses" — calc.state_tax multiplies the supplied PA taxable-income base only. PA Tax Forgiveness (Schedule SP) and other low-income relief are OUTSIDE this flat-rate computation — check Schedule SP eligibility separately. Local earned-income taxes (PA municipalities/school districts) are NOT modeled here.
